site.name: govuk-passport
site.summary: govuk-passport-clone Clone of a GOV.UK-style passport apply / renew multi-step form (one file, multiple steps). Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page multi-step form with section switching: start page (eligibility, fees, required materials) → application type (new / renew / replace) → personal info → address → previous passport info → photo upload → review → stop before payment; step indicator on the left / top; each step has fields, hint text, inline errors, and an error summary; bottom "Save and continue" / "Cancel" | | `styles.css` | GOV.UK Design System style (black-yellow theme, Transport-like font stack, yellow focus outline, red errors) | | `script.js` | Step forward / back, field validation, error-summary focus, state persistence (localStorage) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full govuk-passport system, prioritizing the primary form/onboarding flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The govuk-passport form has a functional multi-step flow with clear progress tracking, but several links (e.g., 'Departments', 'Help', 'News') are misconfigured or non-functional. The photo upload step has a persistent validation error despite file input interactions, and many footer links lack dedicated content. Mobile tap targets are often too small, and some radio buttons/links have unclear functionality.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the govuk-passport system, focusing on the multi-step form flow, state transitions, validation, and recovery paths, across desktop and mobile viewports.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed in phases: start with the initial page and cookie handling, then enter the form flow via 'Start now', progress through each form step (validating navigation, validation, and state persistence), check error handling, and verify mobile responsiveness. Each phase will validate specific interactions and states, with a focus on the single-page form's multi-step navigation and UX patterns.
assumptions: The site is a single-page app with multi-step form navigation handled by JavaScript
LocalStorage is used for state persistence
Form validation includes inline and summary errors

phases.title: Initial Page and Cookie Handling
phases.objective: Validate initial page load, cookie interactions, and 'Start now' button
key_checks: Click 'Accept analytics cookies' and verify state change
Click 'Reject analytics cookies' and verify state change
Click 'Start now ›' and verify navigation to form start

phases.title: Form Navigation (Step Forward/Back)
phases.objective: Validate multi-step form navigation (start, application type, personal info, etc.)
key_checks: Navigate through each form step (start → application type → personal info → address → previous passport → photo upload → review)
Use 'Back' button to return to previous steps
exit_criteria: All form steps visited via forward/back navigation

phases.title: Field Validation and Error Handling
phases.objective: Validate field validation (inline errors) and error summary
key_checks: Submit empty form fields to trigger validation
Verify inline errors and error summary display
Correct errors and verify error removal

phases.title: State Persistence (LocalStorage)
phases.objective: Validate state persistence across form steps and page reloads
key_checks: Fill form fields, navigate steps, and reload page
Verify form state is restored from localStorage
Clear localStorage and verify state reset

phases.title: Mobile Usability (Small Tap Targets)
phases.objective: Validate mobile viewport usability (tap targets, layout)
key_checks: Verify tap targets (e.g., 'Start now', form buttons) meet mobile usability (≥44x44px)
Validate form layout and readability on mobile
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport usability validated (tap targets, layout)

phases.title: Adjacent Flows (Related Content Links)
phases.objective: Validate 'Related content' links (renew, child, lost/stolen, fees)
key_checks: Click 'Renew an adult passport' and verify navigation
Click 'Apply for a child passport' and verify navigation
Click 'Report a lost or stolen passport' and verify navigation

coverage_targets.pages: visit all known HTML pages (only index.html, but explore all form states)
coverage_targets.features: exercise multi-step navigation, field validation, error handling, state persistence, and related links
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks (form navigation, tap targets, layout) on mobile viewport

notes: Focus on the single-page multi-step form (index.html) as the primary flow
Verify small tap targets (mobile usability) for all interactive elements

findings.user_goal: Upload a demo photo to progress the passport application form
findings.problem: The 'Upload a photo' file input (ux-351) fails to resolve the 'Error: Choose a demo photo file' validation error, even after multiple click interactions. The error message persists, and the form cannot progress despite the checkbox being checked and the 'Continue' button being enabled.
findings.evidence: Multiple clicks on the 'Upload a photo' file input (ux-351) in the mobile viewport show no change in the 'Error: Choose a demo photo file' message. The form remains in an error state, preventing progression to the next step.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot complete the photo upload step, blocking the entire application flow. This critical error prevents goal completion and creates frustration.
findings.suggestion: Fix the file input validation logic to recognize demo file selection (e.g., trigger the error only if no file is chosen, or provide clear instructions for demo file upload). Ensure the 'Choose File' interaction properly clears the error and enables form progression.

findings.user_goal: Access dedicated content via footer links (e.g., 'Departments', 'News', 'Help')
findings.problem: Most footer links (e.g., 'Departments', 'News', 'Help', 'Guidance and regulation') navigate to the '#start' section or do nothing, lacking dedicated content. This misconfiguration creates confusion and reduces trust in the site's functionality.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Departments' (ux-177) and 'News' (ux-197) changes the URL to #start but shows no dedicated content. 'Help' (ux-180) and 'Guidance and regulation' (ux-179) have no visible navigation or content change.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect footer links to provide relevant information or navigation, but broken/misconfigured links reduce usability and trust. This creates a disjointed experience and makes the site feel incomplete.
findings.suggestion: Implement dedicated content or correct navigation for footer links (e.g., 'Departments' should link to a departments page, 'News' to a news section). Ensure links either navigate to valid content or are removed if non-functional.
findings.source_hint: index.html: footer links (ux-177, ux-197, ux-180, ux-179)

findings.user_goal: Interact with clickable elements (links, buttons, inputs) on mobile
findings.problem: Many mobile tap targets (e.g., 'GOV.UK local demo home', 'Apply for a passport', 'Home', 'Service') are smaller than the recommended 44x44px, making them difficult to tap accurately. This affects usability for users with motor impairments or on touch devices.
findings.evidence: Mobile viewport analysis shows tap targets like 'GOV.UK local demo home' (142x43px) and 'Apply for a passport' (204x26px) are below the 44px height guidance. Layout warnings confirm small tap targets across multiple footer and header links.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets increase the risk of misclicks, reduce accessibility for users with motor disabilities, and create a frustrating mobile experience. This violates WCAG guidelines and harms usability.
findings.suggestion: Increase the size of mobile tap targets to at least 44x44px (e.g., adjust link/button padding, spacing, or font size). Ensure all interactive elements meet accessibility standards for touch interaction.
findings.source_hint: index.html: mobile viewport (e.g., ux-340, ux-341, ux-342)

findings.problem: The 'Accessibility statement' link (ux-156) navigates to #start (same as 'Home'), lacking dedicated accessibility content. This misconfiguration misleads users and reduces transparency about accessibility features.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Accessibility statement' (ux-156) changes the URL to #start but displays the form's start page, not an accessibility statement. Similar issues exist for 'Privacy' and other support links.
findings.why_it_matters: Users seeking accessibility information or privacy policies cannot find them, violating legal requirements and user expectations. This reduces trust and accessibility compliance.
findings.suggestion: Create dedicated pages or sections for 'Accessibility statement' and 'Privacy' content, or update the links to point to relevant information. Ensure support links provide accurate, accessible content.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to 'Departments' or 'News' content via footer links
findings.problem: Footer links like 'Departments' (ux-177) and 'News' (ux-197) have no visible navigation or content change, or navigate to #start without dedicated content. This creates dead ends and confusion for users exploring site navigation.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Departments' (ux-177) and 'News' (ux-197) shows no URL or content change, or navigates to #start with no dedicated page. The links appear non-functional or misconfigured.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect footer links to provide additional resources or navigation, but broken links reduce usability and create a disjointed experience. This harms the site's credibility and user trust.
findings.suggestion: Fix the href attributes of footer links to point to valid content (e.g., dedicated 'Departments' or 'News' sections) or remove non-functional links. Provide clear navigation paths for all footer elements.

findings.user_goal: Interact with small tap targets on mobile (e.g., radio buttons, links)
findings.problem: Many mobile tap targets (e.g., radio buttons, small links) are smaller than 44x44px, violating mobile usability guidelines. This makes interactions difficult for users with motor impairments or on touch devices.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings show tap targets like the 'I confirm this is a demo photo...' checkbox (40x40px) and footer links (e.g., 'Benefits' 58x17px) are below the 44px height guidance. Radio buttons and small links have similarly small tap areas.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets increase the risk of misclicks, reduce accessibility, and create frustration for mobile users. This violates WCAG and mobile usability best practices.
findings.suggestion: Increase the size of small tap targets (e.g., radio buttons, footer links) to at least 44x44px by adjusting padding, spacing, or font size. Ensure all interactive elements meet mobile touch target guidelines.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to 'Report a lost or stolen passport' content
findings.problem: The 'Report a lost or stolen passport' link (ux-305) navigates to the '#service-start' section (main application form), not a dedicated lost/stolen passport page. This misconfiguration misleads users seeking specific guidance.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Report a lost or stolen passport' (ux-305) changes the URL to #service-start, displaying the main passport application form, not a dedicated lost/stolen page.
findings.why_it_matters: Users seeking help for lost/stolen passports are redirected to the main application form, creating confusion and increasing task time. This misalignment between link text and destination reduces usability.
findings.suggestion: Update the 'Report a lost or stolen passport' link to point to a dedicated page or section with relevant guidance. Ensure link text accurately reflects the destination content.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to 'View cookies' content to understand cookie usage
findings.problem: The 'View cookies' link navigates to #start (form's start page) but displays no cookie details. This misconfiguration prevents users from accessing cookie information, violating transparency expectations.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'View cookies' changes the URL to #start but shows the form's start page, not cookie details. No dedicated cookie information is visible.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot access cookie usage information, violating privacy best practices and user expectations. This reduces transparency and trust in the site.
findings.suggestion: Create a dedicated 'View cookies' section or page with cookie details, or update the link to point to relevant information. Ensure cookie information is accessible and transparent.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to 'News' content via the footer link
findings.problem: The 'News' link (ux-197) navigates to #start (form's start page) but displays no dedicated news content. This misconfiguration creates a dead end for users seeking news updates.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'News' (ux-197) changes the URL to #start but shows the form's start page, not a news page. No news-related content is visible.
findings.why_it_matters: Users seeking news updates are redirected to the form's start page, creating confusion and reducing the site's perceived functionality. This misalignment harms user experience and trust.
findings.suggestion: Update the 'News' link to point to a dedicated news page or section, or remove the link if news content is not available. Ensure footer links provide accurate navigation to relevant content.
